restaurant.summary: Guests come for the coffee and stay for the baking: the flat white and banana bread are the most praised, the staff are called warm and quick, and the usual gripe is that it is busy and seats are scarce.
restaurant.say: Kaffeine is rated 4.6 stars on Google from 2,283 reviews.

cards.author: J FM
cards.text: Lovely small cafe tucked away a few minutes behind the busy Oxford circus. Coffee was ok very small cup, personally wished it was served warmer . They offer a limited selection of baked sweet treats, and they do serve a few breakfast dishes.

cards.author: Nick J.
cards.text: One of the many awesome coffee shops around this part of town. The coffee is spot on - incredible, even - but that means it's super popular... There can sometimes be a little bit of a wait in the morning peak, but the friendly and convivial atmosphere, and that divine coffee that comes at the end of it, makes it totally worthwhile.

cards.author: Kelsey D.
cards.text: This coffee shop was recommended to me by another coffee shop in Dublin, Ireland. On my visit it did not disappoint, the staff were so welcoming and friendly, the coffee was one of the best I've had and the treats were even better! If I'm ever back in London this will be my go to coffee shop! The ice coffee's are amazing too!!!

cards.author: Raheem L.
cards.text: A lovely coffee shop with a welcoming atmosphere. It’s always great to find somewhere that offers a comfortable setting to enjoy a coffee and take a break from a busy day. cards.reply: Hey Raheem, Thanks so much. Hope to see you again soon!…

cards.author: Jennifer M.
cards.text: Great little place that takes coffee and good food seriously. Batch brew (filter coffee) was perfectly balanced and the flat white was awesome as well. cards.text: Definately check this place out. Best coffee we found, single origin beans and great selection of teas. There was also plenty of sweets and delicious lunch options. All reasonably priced and had a great comfy atmosphere. The staff were all very friendly also.
